maxRps.rationale: Prose gives no explicit admission ceiling and current traffic (50 rps) is well below typical gateway limits, so use a large typical default rather than a value near current load.

instances.rationale: Prose states the upload API runs on 6 instances.

concurrencyPerInstance.rationale: No concurrency figure given; a typical stateless API instance handling quick accept-and-enqueue requests supports tens of concurrent requests per instance.

serviceTimeMs.rationale: The API only accepts the file and enqueues a job before returning, explicitly not waiting for transcoding, so service time covers just the accept+enqueue overhead, not the transcode itself.

capacity.rationale: No queue depth stated; using a typical default buffer size for a job queue decoupling bursty uploads from slower workers.

consumers.rationale: Prose states there are 12 worker consumers pulling jobs off the queue.

consumerServiceTimeMs.rationale: Prose emphasizes transcoding is slow and the expensive part of the pipeline but gives no number; a typical media transcode job takes on the order of several seconds to tens of seconds of CPU-bound work.

connectionPoolSize.rationale: Prose states the Postgres pool is capped at 30 connections.

queryTimeMs.rationale: No query latency stated; a simple metadata insert after transcoding is typically fast.

writeRatio.rationale: Prose states workers only write job metadata and nothing else reads from that table in the request path, so all traffic to this database is writes.

readReplicas.rationale: Prose explicitly states there are no read replicas.

replicaApplyRate.rationale: With zero read replicas, there is no replica apply throughput to speak of.
